Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the LEAP India Limited Q2 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there 
will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need

your touchtone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
I now hand the conference over to Ms. Soumya Chhajed from Go India Advisors. Thank you, 
and over to you, ma'am. 
Soumya Chhajed: 
Good day, everyone, and welcome to Q2 and H1 FY27 Earnings Call of LEAP India Limited. 
We have with us Mr. Sunu Mathew – Chairman, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer 
– LEAP India Limited; Mr. Hrishi Gandhi, the Chief Growth Officer; and Mr. Rajesham Alle, 
the Chief Financial Officer. Please be reminded that discussions on today's call may include 
certain forward-looking statements and must be, therefore, viewed in conjunction with the risk 
pertaining to the business. 
I now request the management to provide more insight and post that we'll begin with Q&A. 
Thank you, and over to you. 
Sunu Mathew: 
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to LEAP India Limited's earning conference call for the 
second quarter and first half of FY27. I would like to start with the business overview. For those 
joining us for the first time, LEAP is India's largest on-demand asset pooling company with 
around 90%, 92% share of the organized pallet pooling market. We provide pallets, plastic 
containers, and material handling equipment on a pay-per-use basis.  
 
We take full care of the full asset life cycle, which means deployment, tracking, retrieval, repair, 
and redeployment. Today, we manage a pool of 15.5 million assets valued at over INR1,820 
crores. We serve round about 1,100-plus customers across 11,000 touchpoints through 27 
fulfillment centers.  
 
A detailed overview of the business and the industry opportunity is available in our investor 
presentation. So, today I will focus on what has changed during this quarter, which is the second 
quarter. So, one of the most important announcement that I would like to make is the acquisition 
of Vimprotech and TIPS. 
The most important development this quarter is our agreement to acquire 100% of the business 
of Vimprotech and TIPS for an equity value of INR142 crores. Both are being acquired through 
slump sales into newly incorporated, wholly owned subsidiaries, Vimprotech into Vimprotech 
Private Limited, which will be our manufacturing arm, and TIPS into Total Integrated Packaging 
Solution, that means TIPS Private Limited, which will be our pooling arm.  
 
Vimprotech is into plastic manufacturing, providing end-to-end solution and in-house designing, 
mold-making, and production of vacuum forming and injection molding across its two plants in 
Puducherry and Tamil Nadu. TIPS is a crate and tray pooling business, predominantly very 
strong in the automotive sector, with an asset pool of 0.25 million crates and trays.

Together with a robust customer base of 200-plus, they have reported FY26 revenue at INR61.7 
crores at an EBITDA margin of 28%, with revenue growing up to 44% CAGR over the last three 
years. The strategic logic is straightforward. First, it gives us backward integration into plastics, 
boosting our innovation and building newer capabilities. This will result in reducing our 
dependence on outside vendors, improving turnaround time, quality control, and cost.  
 
Second, it increases our portfolio and leverages our customer base to cross-sell. Third, it adds a 
strong Southern footprint that we can scale through our existing network in the West and North. 
And you understand that 30% to 40% of the business of automobile is in the South part of the 
country. On an FY26 pro forma basis, the transaction is accretive to revenue, EBITDA, and 
PAT, and improves our net debt to EBITDA.  
 
We are pleased to announce that we have already signed the BTA on 26th October. The key 
managerial persons will continue to be associated with us, ensuring leadership continuity and a 
seamless transition. I understand that there has been a lot of questions on GCC expansion. So, 
we have set up wholly owned subsidiaries in Saudi Arabia and the UAE. 
The GCC is a natural extension of our platform. Palletization levels are already high, automation 
and ASRS adoption are rising, and the movement hire model is very well-understood. We 
continue to take a measured, phased approach to this market. We are contemplating certain 
acquisitions also in the GCC market. 
A stronger balance sheet is the third point that I want to put forward. From our IPO fresh issue 
of INR480 crores, INR360 crores has been used to repay debt. On a post-IPO basis, our debt to 
equity is about 0.5, and our net debt to EBITDA is about 1.9x, with around INR110 crores held 
as investments. This gives us the flexibility to pursue value-accretive opportunities such as this 
acquisition while staying disciplined on the leverage. 
I am very happy to announce that in the month of October, India Ratings and Research, a Fitch 
Group company, upgraded LEAP's long-term rating from A to A plus, and same has happened 
for TARON business, which is our MHE business, that has also moved from A to A plus. 
This is our third upgrade in about 3.5 years. We now have a leaner balance sheet, a top-tier short-
term rating, and a clear runway to fund the next leg of growth, including value-accretive 
opportunities, such as this acquisition, while staying disciplined on the leverage. 
Let me come to the certain performance highlights. I would like to tell you that always when 
you look at this business, you should compare it over last year, so quarter-on-quarter is -- we are 
not a selling company. So, you cannot compare it with quarter 1 to quarter 2 because this is a 
seasonal business. 
So, as compared to last year's quarter 2, we have done INR216 crores of turnover. We have 
grown by 22.5%. We have done INR110 crores of EBITDA, which is we have grown by 24.8%. 
Overall EBITDA for the first half is 52.2%.

integrate Vimprotech and TIPS, and build the GCC business in a measured way. We will do this 
with continued discipline on asset utilization, returns on capital, and balance sheet strength.

the quarter.

network synergies from CHEP integration, where our fulfilment centres were close to erstwhile 
CHEP facilities. We consolidated with them, closing two facilities and bringing our network to 
27 fulfilment centres without any loss of reach. 
With regard to movement hire, there is a constant improvement in movement hire business, and 
we are converting customers from dairy sector, textile sectors from static hire to the movement 
hire, and the journey will continue further.

allotment fee, daily rental, and increasingly, movement fee at each leg of supply chain.
